title: Emergent Fermi Surfaces in Periodically Driven Bose Gases
authors: Li-kun Shi, Oles Matsyshyn, Inti Sodemann Villadiego
abstract: We show that the steady state of a periodically driven Bose gas coupled to a thermal bath features emergent Fermi surfaces both in its high temperature and Bose-Einstein-condensate (BEC) states. These emergent Fermi surfaces are non-analyticities in the occupation function as a function of momentum arising from the lack of detailed balance of collisions away from equilibrium. They are stronger in the BEC than in the normal gas, and can be more robust against finite temperature smearing than the usual equilibrium Fermi surfaces of Fermi gases. We also show that they give rise to analogous rich phenomena, such as Friedel oscillations in the density correlations and quantum oscillations in response to applied magnetic fields controlled by their areas, albeit with marked quantitative differences. Our results establish non-equilibrium conditions as a promising alternative pathway to achieve the long-sought-after emergence of Fermi surfaces in bosonic system. We outline strategies to experimentally discover these exotic states in ultra-cold atomic clouds.
summary: This work demonstrates that periodically driving a Bose gas out of equilibrium can induce emergent Fermi surfaces, characterized by non-analyticities in momentum space. These signatures manifest as observable long-range oscillations in the density correlations. The findings establish non-equilibrium dynamics as a powerful route to realizing Fermi liquid physics in bosonic quantum gases.
main_problem: The study investigates the emergence of Fermi surfaces in bosonic systems that are driven out of equilibrium by periodic forces.
main_result: Non-equilibrium driving conditions can induce non-analyticities in the momentum occupation function, mimicking Fermi surfaces, even in weakly interacting bosons.
method: The analysis uses the Floquet-Boltzmann equation to model the steady-state occupation function and calculates density correlations via Fourier transforms.
model_or_system: The model is a weakly interacting Bose gas coupled to a thermal bath and subjected to a time-periodic driving force, analyzed in both BEC and normal gas regimes.
key_observables: Non-analyticities (jumps) in the momentum occupation function $f_p$, Friedel oscillations in density correlations $C_B(r)$, and quantum oscillations in response to magnetic fields.
important_parameters: Driving frequency ($\Omega$), bath temperature ($T_B$), and driving amplitude ($A_0$).
main_assumptions: The analysis relies on the weak coupling limit to derive the Floquet-Boltzmann equation and assumes the existence of distinct non-analytic features corresponding to Fermi surface signatures.
figures_summary: Figures illustrate the phase diagram, schematic occupation functions comparing equilibrium vs. driven states, and the spatial decay of density correlations showing oscillatory behavior.
paper_structure: The paper progresses by establishing the non-equilibrium framework via the Floquet-Boltzmann equation, identifying the momentum-space signatures (non-analyticities), and then calculating the corresponding real-space fingerprints (density correlations and kinetic energy oscillations).
why_interesting: It provides a concrete, non-equilibrium mechanism for generating Fermi surface physics in bosonic systems, which is a long-standing goal in the field, offering experimental pathways using ultra-cold atoms.
